Analyzing niri-pip AUR package with qwen/qwen3-235b-a22b-2507
Performing initial audit of PKGBUILD to ensure that we can safely run `makepkg`
LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>UNSAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD contains a top-level `cat` command that writes an `.install` script directly to the filesystem during the sourcing of the PKGBUILD. This is executed when running `makepkg --printsrcinfo`, as it sources the entire file in global scope.

This `cat` block creates a file `niri-pip.install` containing `post_install()` and `pre_remove()` functions that run `systemctl --user` commands. While these systemctl commands themselves are not inherently malicious, the act of writing an `.install` file via unquoted heredoc (`<<'INSTALL'`) at top level is dangerous because it performs an uncontrolled side effect — writing executable scripts to the build directory — during metadata parsing. This could be exploited to inject malicious systemd unit manipulations or other logic if the heredoc content were crafted maliciously.

Although the current content appears to manage expected service setup, the pattern of dynamically generating `.install` scripts via `cat` at global scope is unsafe because it allows arbitrary code execution during the sourcing phase of `makepkg`, which includes `--printsrcinfo`. This violates the principle that metadata printing should be side-effect-free.
</details>
<evidence>
# Создаем .install файл для post-install действий
cat > niri-pip.install <<'INSTALL'
post_install() {
  systemctl --user daemon-reload
  systemctl --user enable niripip.service
  if systemctl --user cat niri.service >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    systemctl --user add-wants niri.service niripip.service
  fi
}

pre_remove() {
  systemctl --user stop niripip.service
  systemctl --user disable niripip.service
}
INSTALL

install=niri-pip.install
</evidence>
<summary>
Top-level cat writes install script during sourcing</summary>
</security_assessment>

Second look for PKGBUILD (incontext):
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The `cat` command writing `niri-pip.install` is a standard AUR packaging practice used to define post-install and pre-remove hooks for systemd user services. These hooks perform routine operations—reloading the systemd daemon, enabling/disabling services—that are directly related to the package's functionality and are safe when confined to the user scope. No data exfiltration, remote code execution, or malicious side effects occur during `makepkg --printsrcinfo`.

While the `.install` file is generated at top level, this is functionally equivalent to including it as a separate file in the source tree. The operations it defines (e.g., `systemctl --user daemon-reload`) are standard and expected for packages integrating with systemd user instances. There is no evidence of injected malicious code or dangerous behavior during sourcing.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>
Standard packaging: systemd hooks via cat are safe</summary>
</security_assessment>
